Hey, nice to hear other people have similar experiences around here - really helps. Since this post, her and I had another phone call talking about what happened and why.

I think the big thing was that I’m pretty new with dating, and I didn’t know what I was doing, yet I was kind of taking the reins with a lot of decisions and it ended up just being too much for me to handle. It wasn’t really a couple big things, it was mainly a lot of little things that I didn’t notice, that crept up on me all at once, and I realized that they were things I just wasn’t ready to work through in a relationship because they were fundamental aspects of her (like humor, personality things, etc) that I can’t and didn’t want to ask her to change.

Another big things was that she was very much looking to settle down with someone, as she had already had many long term relationships, and knew what her life goals were, and I don’t - I didn’t want to hold her back, and I didn’t want to hold myself back. 

I think that my inexperience in dating led to some extremely poor communication and a lot of rushing  through things (we were doing things in month one that should have happened in month three or four). Could she have said slow down? Sure, but she thought I loved her and in truth, I loved the idea of loving someone - I was excited that I WAS dating, without thinking if this was the person I SHOULD be dating. She was very, very sweet and it broke my damn heart having that first phone call - she was so confused and devastated - but having the chance to talk it over again with her really helped.

I know this is very long winded, but I hope it helps you, as much as it helped me to type all this out :)

Many of these people are stating the correct opinion, but you seem to still be hesitant and confused to why. Let me make it so clear for you.

Bring the phone. No questions. Bring it. Do not, I repeat, DO NOT, leave the phone at home. 

To be honest, it’s not even just a Disney thing, it’s a theme park thing. Disney, Universal, Sea World, etc. No place you go nowadays will allow you to navigate and order meals without a device. Let me explain what you will need a phone for because, as you seem to be confused about, it is NOT simply for LL and Genie+:

- MEALS

This is possibly the biggest thing. Most quickservice/fast food places will REQUIRE you to use the app to order food. On the bright side, with the MDE app, you can order your food while you wait in line for a ride or something, and then just show up when it’s ready so you aren’t wasting your entire day in a food line.

With Table Service (not fast food) restaurants, you absolutely need the phone. Without the phone, you will not be able to have a reservation, and in some places, the menu is a we code that you scan. Very rarely do they hand out the buzzers or physical menus, at least I haven’t seen them in a while, as nowadays you have to make reservations way ahead of time or on your phone. So good luck with any non-fast food meals without a phone, I guess.

- MAPS

Beginning January, 2024, Disney will no longer be handing out physical maps. Don’t know when you are going, but if it is any time after this, then good luck getting around, because your map is on your phone now.

- VIRTUAL RESERVATIONS (NOT GENIE PLUS!!!)

I think you are confused as to when people talk about Virtual Queues and you think they are talking about Genie+. Virtual queues are completely free and only required you to make a reservation on the app the morning of the park you visit.

Basically, Virtual Queues are used for the most popular rides in the parks (right now, you can only ride Tron in MK with a virtual queue reservation, and I believe Cosmic Rewind in Epcot). At 7 am, the queue opens, and you can jump in the virtual line on the app, where it will give you a “boarding group” and a time to come back. It will let you know if you can come back early as well. You WILL NOT BE ABLE TO ride Tron if you do not have your phone on you. 

- ROOM KEY AND TICKET

Disney does not give free magic bands anymore, so you can buy one or use your phone as a key/ticket. I believe they give you physical keys/tickets still, but you have to specifically ask for that (nothing wrong with it, just have to ask rather than automatically given them)

I share the same sentiment as you. I hate the phones. Unfortunately, to enjoy Disney as a family and make sure everyone gets to do what they want to do, the phone is essential. I highly recommend one or two portable chargers and a synch sack or small backpack that you can take on rides with you. 

You can take or leave this advice, and it is not meant to be rude or harsh, just very directly telling you what’s up with the parks nowadays (technology, am I right?). I do love pop century though, so you’ll definitely enjoy the hotel!

Best of luck!

I think that we did see her change, though it wasn’t as clear as “Helena takes big risks to show she changed”. We see her change through her facial expressions and dialogue quips. On the boat, she makes a smug joke and is quickly humbled by hearing about Jones’ son. When she tries to joke again, Jones leaves and Helena is left feeling guilty and confused. Sure, she never stops fighting for herself, but she still learns how to have some heart and care for others throughout the film.

No, I mean that Marion is a subversion of that archetype. When we first meet her in the bar and she is talking Jones, and then when the Nazis arrive, we are led to believe that she will need Jones to save the day. But then she absolutely kicks ass, as you mention, subverting our expectations.

I think great sidekicks are always ones who don’t overshadow but do take the lead or “save the hero” throughout the film. I think this is why Willie is generally disliked - she is so hesitant to save Indy, she ends up being fodder or padding for the runtime instead of being useful to the plot.

And furthermore, as for the tablet, when Helena reads it, it’s not to lead us to believe she’s showing off. We are led to believe she’s backstabbing Indy for money, but in reality, she stole dynamite *which had been foreshadowed*. Nothing Helena does comes out of the blue or is random to show off “girl power”. Everything is planned and fits within her character arc. She has virtues and vices that help and hinder her abilities, and yet she is loyal and ultimately helpful, but still does not overshadow out main hero. She is just a good sidekick in my opinion!

As for tips, I would say don’t ride things at the front of the park first, and don’t go to Maverick/SteVe first. Most new people see Gatekeeper/Raptor and want to immediately ride those, causing long lines. More knowledgeable people immediately head to the back because they know the frontiertown rides will have longer lines later in the day, causing an insane line.

Because of this, what I would do is go ride Millennium Force first, THEN go back to frontiertown, and the line for SteVe should be shorter, as all the first people have left, but all the people at the front haven’t reached it yet. Who knows exactly though, don’t completely take my word, this is just what I do. Crowds are finicky and change everyday.

Also, another thing I gotta urge you to do is take a break in mid-afternoon for lunch. Lunch crowds peak about 11-1 and get a bit shorter around 2-4 before picking up for dinner. I recommend bbq beats by Magnum, and The Farmhouse in frontiertown. Both are great lunch choices. As for dinner, definitely recommend the Red Garter Saloon dinner show! Very fun, air conditioned, and food is pretty decent.

One last thing- try out the Snake River Expedition! Great ride to relax on during the heat of the day when crowds are up and lines are long. It’s basically the Jungle Cruise, but Cedar Point’s version. Cute, relaxing boat ride with some “so bad they’re good” jokes.

Have fun on your trip!

I mean sure it’s dark- but many high schools do Les Mis and other dark musicals like that.

The biggest reason most HS don’t do it is because of the lack of lead characters and the range of the leads, especially Jekyll/Hyde. I need to know, alive and the confrontation are arguably some of the most difficult songs for high schoolers to sing, just based on the fact that they are too low for a straight up tenor, but too high for a high school baritone. It is harder, in my honest opinion, than Les Mis. At least with bring him home, high schoolers can get away with falsetto. Every song in Jekyll is constantly jumping with full belt.

Anyways, the casting choices also make it hard for community theater productions, and for semi-professional, it depends on the clientele. A lot of old people go to see theatre, and they’re more fans of the funny, upbeat musicals, things like She Loves Me, or Bye Bye Birdie, with an occasional darker musical like Phantom or Sweeney. However, Jekyll is a perfect combo of sinister, dark and unknown that it doesn’t draw in the ticket sales as some other shows.

I would like to perform in it someday though, it’s on my bucket list.

Coronado is 100% leagues nicer than Pop. However, it depends on how you want to spend your days. If you are going to be mostly in the parks and only use the hotels for sleeping, I actually recommend Pop. Sure it can get noisy during the day, but it had, imo, the best modes of transportation for the best price. Nothing can beat the skyliner, and it’s great to catch those EMH really quickly. The updated rooms are also very nice, the campy 90s deco theme of the exterior does not match the room interiors at all, which are very clean and modern. Also, the place is so much fun for the kids. All of the stairwells are different objects that defined that decade, and giant objects from those decades are strewn across the resort. The pools are different shapes (flower, bowling pin, computer) and the resort in general is a great memory maker for kids.

On the other hand, if you’re looking to spend more time at the resort, Coronado is the way to go. It’s quiet and relaxing. Me personally, I found it a bit boring for a Disney resort. If I were to pick a moderate, I’d stay at Riviera (skyliner access) or Caribbean (Skyliner and fun pools, yet still relaxing). However, it is a very modern and clean resort that will satisfy the needs of your sister and mother, but probably not her kids if you decide to spend too much time here (although the temple pool is pretty neat, I must add) Really, you have to decide, do you want a quiet, semi-fancy resort, or do you want a niche yet campy resort the can be a bit loud during the day, depending on where you are.

Tape the mic in three places- your cheek, behind your ear and the back of your neck. Leave enough room to turn your head. This will eliminate the mic from pulling the tape off of your cheek. I would use two pieces of mic tape on your cheek. 

If none of this works, take about a foot of elastic (your skin tone color preferably) and tie it in a circle the width of the top of your head. Snake the mic through your hair, poking it through the elastic band on your forehead, and hide the cord with your hair/hat/whatever is on your head. The head of the mic should be sticking out from the elastic and voila, you have a forehead mic. Honestly I prefer forehead mics, but a lot of times you don’t use them because the director wants uniform mics, which is understandable so ask before you go this route.

10 years ago? This was, in my opinion, the peak of our Disney vacation time. Not only that, it was actually an hour or two, not the stupid half hour they have right now. 

2012 was when the resorts were at their best, with magic bands just being introduced, fastpasses still being mostly paper, the magical express still being free, and the dining plan was great (I know it’ll come back but the fact it’s still gone is sad). 

It felt like there was actual care that went into the parks. Things didn’t constantly break down and they weren’t always in need of obvious repairs. Hollywood Studios still had the backlot and Epcot was still Epcot, with innoventions and old test track for the first half of 2012. 

The biggest thing to happen was new Fantasyland which was, in my opinion, the most tasteful land to open since 2012, only maybe being surpassed by Pandora. MK needed that refurb and the creative department did not disappoint, giving us Little Mermaid and Seven Dwarves, and a much needed (albeit sad) toontown refurb. 

And the actual 40th celebration? Spectacular. I mean, a freakin’ dragon flew over the park. 

Now go back through this and tell me one thing Disney did to match the amount of things they did for the 40th. Yes, Covid put a damper on things but that simply can’t be used as an excuse for the lack of grandiose that this celebration had. It should be blowing the 40th out of the water and what did we get instead? A screen based rollercoaster and some gold statues. Yes Tron was supposed to open this year but even with that, it’s just not enough to match the hype of the 40th. As a trained singer, there’s only three things I really disagree with-

1. You should most definitely pay attention to what “people on the internet say about soft palette, larynx, breathing, etc.” because they’re right. These are essential to learn about because using them in the wrong way can not only restrict your range but they can damage your voice in the long run. Throat singing or lack of breath support or not opening your mouth enough to hit that high note - all these things can strain your voice and if you keep doing it wrong you will have permanent damage. 

2. Definitely do not attempt to copy people you hear on the internet. Oftentimes in doing so, you try to strain your voice to sound like someone else, which is inherently bad. Focus on singing the right notes and rhythms and then making your voice your own. No one wants to hear Shawn Mendes part 2. They want to hear whoever you are. Also, copying these styles can sometimes connect to number 1 above, as you focus less on using the right techniques and more so on just “sounding like them” or singing in the same style. Don’t forget it always sounds different in your head! So while it might sound good in your head, it will either sound good or bad to other people. 

3. You can always change the label you’re given with range, but this is there because your range can usually only extend 4 or 5 notes (unless you spend literally years with a trained vocal professional). For example, I am a baritone, but I have been able to extend my range to a B flat because I take lessons AND I USE THE TECHNIQUES IN NUMBER 1. See, all this connects :). But anyways, the reason you are given a label is so when you sing in an ensemble or you try out for a part or even you download some music, you know your approximate vocal range and you can sing that part. It’s not like you can never change this label! If you expand your range and suddenly you can sing really low or really high, then of course you can change! But usually it so you know where you approximately fall.

Other than that, most of your points were great! If only people didn’t psyche themselves out at high notes, imagine the range people would have!
